input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: Calling `.strip()` removes prompt whitespace as well as ANSI codes, including the trailing space separating a prompt from the user's input.
- rationale: When stdout is redirected or otherwise does not support ANSI, a prompt such as `Name: ` becomes `Name:`. Leading whitespace used for indentation is also removed, so users and output consumers see altered prompt formatting. `strip_ansi(text)` alone preserves the intended whitespace.
critique: The finding identifies the same mechanism: `.strip()` applied after ANSI stripping removes the prompt's trailing space when the stream is non-color, so 'Name: ' becomes 'Name:'. This matches the label's root cause and failure path.
